services.name: n8n
services.description: Run and build the client's n8n workflows.
notes: In n8n, an owner or admin turns on MCP access under Settings > Instance-level MCP, then switches on each workflow the AI may use. Workflows that aren't switched on stay invisible.

fields.label: The client's n8n address
fields.help: The address you open n8n at. You can also paste the full MCP address from n8n's Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect a client.

fields.label: The client's n8n address
fields.help: The address you open n8n at. You can also paste the full MCP address from n8n's Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect a client.

fields.label: MCP access token
fields.help: In n8n: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect a client > API key. Making a new token replaces the old one.

services.name: Supabase
services.description: Query and manage the client's Supabase projects.
notes: When signing in, pick the client's organization, the one that owns their project.

fields.label: Project ID (optional)
fields.help: Keeps the AI to one project. In Supabase: Project Settings > General > Project ID. Leave empty to allow all the client's projects.

fields.label: Access token
fields.help: Create one while signed in as the client's Supabase account.

fields.label: Project ID (optional)
fields.help: Keeps the AI to one project. In Supabase: Project Settings > General > Project ID.

services.name: Airtable
services.description: Read and update the client's Airtable bases.

fields.label: Personal access token
fields.help: The link opens Airtable with the right permissions ticked. Choose which of the client's bases the AI may use, then create the token.

services.name: Notion
services.description: Search, read and write the client's Notion pages.
notes: Sign in with the client's Notion account and choose their workspace. Guests can't connect, and a workspace admin can turn this off.

services.name: Stripe
services.description: Look up and manage the client's Stripe customers, payments and invoices.
notes: Some actions, like refunds, wait for a person to approve them in the Stripe Dashboard. After approving, ask the AI to try again.

options.label: Use a restricted key with agent access

fields.label: Restricted key with agent access
fields.help: In the client's Stripe Dashboard: Developers > API keys > Create restricted key, and choose "Authorizing agent access to your account". It starts with rk_live_ (or rk_test_ for a sandbox).
fields.patternHint: That doesn't look like a restricted key. It should start with rk_live_ or rk_test_.

reject.message: That's a secret key. Stripe no longer accepts those for AI tools. Create a restricted key with agent access instead (it starts with rk_live_).
That's a publishable key, which can't do anything here. Create a restricted key with agent access instead (it starts with rk_live_).

services.name: Neon
services.description: Query and manage the client's Neon Postgres databases.
notes: The AI's database changes run as the database owner unless you pick a smaller role when you sign in. For a live database, consider a role that can only read.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: Create one while signed in to the client's Neon account, ideally limited to the client's organization.

services.name: Netlify
services.description: Deploy and manage the client's Netlify sites.
notes: The AI can deploy sites and change their settings. Sign in with an account that only reaches this client's team.

services.name: GitHub
services.description: Read and work on the client's GitHub repositories, issues and pull requests.
notes: GitHub doesn't let apps sign in by themselves here, so it uses a token. A fine-grained token limited to the client's repositories is safest.

fields.label: Fine-grained token
fields.help: Create it for the client's organization, choose only their repositories, and give it the permissions the AI needs. It starts with github_pat_.
fields.patternHint: That doesn't look like a GitHub token. It should start with github_pat_.

fields.label: Fine-grained token
fields.help: The AI can look but not change anything, whatever the token allows. It starts with github_pat_.
fields.patternHint: That doesn't look like a GitHub token. It should start with github_pat_.

services.name: Apollo
services.description: Find and enrich contacts and companies in the client's Apollo account.
notes: Some actions, like revealing emails or phone numbers, use the client's Apollo credits.

services.name: Leadfeeder
services.description: See which companies visit the client's website, with Leadfeeder by Dealfront.
notes: Needs a paid Leadfeeder plan: on the free plan only sign-in works.
Sign in as a user who has the Manage API keys and Use API permissions. Some lookups use credits.

services.name: Upwork
services.description: Search jobs and talent, and manage proposals, contracts and messages on Upwork.
notes: The AI can send proposals and messages for the account you sign in with, so check what it plans before saying yes.

services.name: Retell AI
services.description: Manage the client's Retell voice agents, phone numbers and calls.
notes: The AI can place real phone calls and buy numbers, which cost money. Use one key per client workspace.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: In the client's Retell dashboard: Settings > API Keys > create a key.

services.name: Twilio
services.description: Send texts, look up numbers and manage calls and phone numbers in the client's Twilio account.
notes: Texts and calls it makes are charged to the client's Twilio account.
This is Twilio's own early version. It covers Twilio's main features: texts, calls and phone numbers.

fields.label: Account SID
fields.patternHint: It starts with AC, followed by 32 letters and numbers.
fields.help: On the client's Twilio Console home page, under Account Info.

fields.label: API key SID
fields.patternHint: It starts with SK, followed by 32 letters and numbers.
fields.help: In the Twilio Console: API keys & tokens > Create API key, type Standard. Copy the SID that starts with SK.

fields.label: API key secret
fields.help: Shown once, right after you create the key. If it's lost, create a new key.

services.name: Make
services.description: Run the client's Make scenarios and see how they went.

services.name: Zapier
services.description: Use the actions set up in the client's Zapier account.
notes: In Zapier, choose which actions the AI may use. Each action it runs uses Zapier tasks.

services.name: GoHighLevel
services.description: Work with contacts, conversations, opportunities and calendars in the client's GoHighLevel sub-account.
notes: You pick the sub-account when you sign in. Sign in once per client sub-account.

services.name: Pipedrive
services.description: Work with the client's Pipedrive deals, people, organizations and activities.

services.name: monday.com
services.description: Read and update the client's monday.com boards and items.
notes: monday.com's server is in beta. One of its tools can do anything the monday.com API allows, so check what the AI plans before saying yes.

services.name: Close
services.description: Work with the client's Close leads, contacts, opportunities and tasks.
notes: You choose what the AI may do when you sign in.

services.name: Klaviyo
services.description: Work with the client's Klaviyo profiles, lists, campaigns and flows.
notes: Sign in as an Owner, Admin or Manager of the client's Klaviyo account.

services.name: Resend
services.description: Send email and manage domains, contacts and broadcasts in the client's Resend account.
notes: The AI can send real email from the client's domains.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: Create one in the client's Resend account. It starts with re_.
fields.patternHint: That doesn't look like a Resend key. It should start with re_.

services.name: WordPress.com
services.description: Read and write posts, pages and comments on the client's WordPress.com sites.
notes: One sign-in reaches every site on that WordPress.com account. Choose Read only when you sign in if that's all you need.

services.name: WordPress (own site)
services.description: Read and write posts and pages on a WordPress site the client hosts themselves.
notes: The site needs WordPress 6.9 or later with the WordPress MCP Adapter plugin installed.
Use an application password (Users > Profile > Application passwords), not the account's real password.

fields.label: The site's MCP address
fields.help: The MCP Adapter plugin shows it. It's usually the site address followed by /wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server.
fields.patternHint: Use the full address that starts with https://

fields.label: WordPress username
fields.help: The user the application password belongs to.

fields.label: Application password
fields.help: In the client's WordPress admin: Users > Profile > Application passwords > Add new.

services.name: Webflow
services.description: Read and update the client's Webflow sites, pages and CMS items.
notes: You pick which sites the AI may use when you sign in.

services.name: Wix
services.description: Manage the client's Wix site: content, products, bookings and more.
notes: Two of Wix's tools can call any part of the Wix API, so check what the AI plans before saying yes.

services.name: PayPal
services.description: Look up and manage the client's PayPal invoices, orders, payments and disputes.
notes: Refunds and payouts move real money. Try it with a PayPal sandbox account first.

services.name: Trello
services.description: Read and update the client's Trello boards, lists and cards.

services.name: Jira and Confluence
services.description: Work with the client's Jira issues and Confluence pages.
notes: You pick the client's Atlassian site when you sign in. The AI's requests use the site's Rovo credits.

options.label: Sign in with Jira and Confluence

services.name: Linear
services.description: Work with the client's Linear issues, projects and cycles.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: Create a personal API key while signed in to the client's Linear workspace. It starts with lin_api_.
fields.patternHint: That doesn't look like a Linear key. It should start with lin_api_.

services.name: Canva
services.description: Find, create and edit designs in the client's Canva account.

services.name: Calendly
services.description: See and manage the client's Calendly event types, bookings and availability.

services.name: Cal.com
services.description: See and manage the client's Cal.com bookings, event types and schedules.

services.name: Tavily
services.description: Search the web and read pages, with Tavily.
notes: Each search uses Tavily credits.

services.name: Apify
services.description: Run Apify scrapers and other Actors, and read their results.
notes: Running an Actor uses the account's Apify credits.

fields.label: API token
fields.help: In Apify: Settings > API & Integrations. It starts with apify_api_.
fields.patternHint: That doesn't look like an Apify token. It should start with apify_api_.

services.name: ElevenLabs
services.description: Make speech, clone voices and manage voice agents and calls in the client's ElevenLabs account.
notes: Speech, voice clones and calls use the client's ElevenLabs credits.
Audio it makes is saved on this computer, in the Desktop folder.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: In the client's ElevenLabs account: Developers > API keys > Create key. Give it only the permissions the AI needs.
